en: 3. The Maṇikaṇṭha Jātaka “Abundant and excellent food and drink arise for me because of this jewel.”
I will not give that to you, for you are an excessive beggar;
nor shall I come to your hermitage,
like a well-trained horse with hands washed clean of grit.
Though you entreated me, begging for the rock,
you terrified me; therefore, I will not give it to you,
for you are one who begs excessively, nor will I come to your hermitage.
“One should not beg from one whom one wishes to hold dear;
one becomes an object of contempt through excessive begging.
When the Naga was asked for his jewel by the brahmin, [he gave it].”
Thus ends the third Jātaka, the Maṇikaṇṭha Jātaka.
